title: They do: -vat or -vät
focus: Choose and attach -vat or -vät to a verb stem that is always supplied.

exercises.prompt: puhua (“to speak”): puhu- + -vat → ____ (“they speak”)
exercises.explanation: puhua means “to speak”; puhuvat means “they speak”. The stem puhu- is supplied. For he (“they”), vowel harmony selects -vat: puhuvat.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: Subject (who does it) + verb (what they do)

parts.role: Subject — the people doing the action.
parts.formation: he is already the basic pronoun meaning “they”, so it does not need an ending here.

parts.role: Verb — the action performed by the plural subject.
parts.formation: The exercise supplies the stem puhu-, so no stem-building rule is being tested. Add -vat; this ending shows that the subject is he (“they”). Vowel harmony chooses -vat because the supplied stem contains a back vowel: a, o, or u.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: Third-person plural -vat/-vät: form not yet correct

exercises.prompt: Which ending completes supplied asu- from asua (“to live”) to mean “they live”?
exercises.explanation: asua means “to live”; asuvat means “they live”. The stem asu- is supplied. For he (“they”), vowel harmony selects -vat: asuvat.

optionFeedback.-vat: Correct. asua means “to live”; asuvat means “they live”. The stem asu- is supplied. For he (“they”), vowel harmony selects -vat: asuvat.
optionFeedback.-vät: “-vät” does not show the required pattern. asua means “to live”; asuvat means “they live”. The stem asu- is supplied. For he (“they”), vowel harmony selects -vat: asuvat.
